newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent drifts, NYMEX gasoline still supportive.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent drifts, NYMEX gasoline still supportive.

text.p: IPE oil futures drifted sideways on Thursday, holding onto gasoline-inspired strength and cagey about the effect of U.S. product contract expiries, brokers said.

At 1300 gmt IPE September Brent was up three cents at $19.00 a barrel, on the brink of breaking through resistance at the $19 mark. The front-month contract rose 38 cents on Wednesday on the back of the U.S gasoline market.
IPE gas oil gained 75 cents to $171.75 a tonne in early trade and stuck there. All eyes were on the opening of the New York market where August product contracts expire today.
Brokers were divided on the effect of the expiries, with many convinced that September gasoline will continue August's strength and help power the oil complex further forward.
"I don't think that September will be as strong as the August contract," one broker said. "But I do think we'll start to see September pull away from the rest of the board."

Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research said in his daily report, "it's difficult to predict price action ahead of the price expiry as usual, but standing in front of this contract would have been devestating in recent days."

August unleaded was up more than half a cent on ACCESS trading, suggesting vigour remained in the bull run on gasoline, which was kicked off by industry data showing big stock draws and by production problems at some refining plant.

But the shadow of Iraq could also fall on the futures market. U.N. officials are expected to approve soon an aid distribution plan that will clear the way for resumed crude exports that will pull prices lower.
"If there is no news the market will go up," said one broker. "But if there is any hint of bearish news on Iraq it will come off 30 points straight away."
"I think we'll keep ticking up slowly but we'll have to see how New York reacts," said another.
ACCESS trade pushed U.S. crude futures higher, with technical analysts noting little to stop the contract reaching $22 a barrel, barring news on Iraq.
